news.title: Codex moved from desk software to pocket supervision.
news.summary: OpenAI says Codex is now in the ChatGPT mobile app, with live project context, approvals, screenshots, terminal output, diffs, and test results flowing from the Mac host to the phone.
news.why_it_matters: For the singularity tracker, this is not just a convenience feature. It makes longer-running agents easier to keep alive during normal human motion: commute, classroom, coffee, errands, and quick approvals from the phone.

news.title: Figure F.03 remains the embodied signal because endurance beats choreography.
news.summary: The strongest robotics evidence this week is still the public work-shift format: a long Figure F.03 stream and secondary reports around an eight-hour autonomous warehouse-style run.
news.why_it_matters: A beautiful demo clip is weak evidence. A long stream exposes boring details: pauses, repeated manipulation, stalls, recovery, and whether the robot can keep moving after novelty wears off.

news.title: ChatGPT adds a personal finance preview for US Pro users.
news.summary: ChatGPT says Pro users in the U.S. can securely connect financial accounts, see where their money is going, and ask questions based on the information they choose to connect.
news.why_it_matters: A deployment step into a high-stakes domain. Finance forces real permissions, trust, and auditability — a prerequisite for agents operating on your behalf.

news.title: Agent economics became the live fight; Wu interview moved it from metering to proactivity.
news.summary: Axios framed the Anthropic/OpenAI fight as the end of all-you-can-eat agent usage. Anthropic says a SpaceX compute deal doubles Claude Code five-hour limits. The load-bearing primary is TechCrunch (Lucas Ropek, May 13), an on-record interview with Anthropic Claude Code product lead Cat Wu: the next big thing is proactivity. Claude understands what you work on, and just sets up some of these automations for you.
news.why_it_matters: Agent capability is now inseparable from metering AND from what the agent decides to do without being asked. Wu proactivity frame moves the load-bearing question from how much can I use it to how much is it allowed to act for me. That is the same surface where long-horizon work budget actually gets spent.
news.correction: Morning fire cited an Ars Technica URL that does not resolve and a fabricated quote. Replaced with TechCrunch primary by Lucas Ropek, May 13.

news.title: Anthropic + Gates Foundation: 200M USD, four years, AI aimed at the 4.6 billion underserved.
news.summary: Anthropic and the Gates Foundation announced a four-year, 200 million USD partnership covering grant funding, Claude usage credits, and technical support across global health, life sciences, education, agriculture, and economic mobility, plus shared public goods (datasets, benchmarks, infrastructure).
news.why_it_matters: Largest non-revenue AI capital commitment of 2026 and a deployment-coverage anchor structurally separate from the frontier-capability race. A curve event in the embedded-at-scale and AI-doing-science dimensions, not in the leaderboard race.

news.title: DeepMind: the mouse pointer is the wrong UI for an agent-era OS.
news.summary: DeepMind argues the cursor is obsolete UI for a world where agents act on your behalf. The pointer becomes a handoff surface between human attention and agent action.
news.why_it_matters: Pairs with the Cat Wu proactivity frame the same week: two frontier labs publicly arguing the next UI primitive is what does the agent do without being asked. The slow-burn variable behind the agent-economics fight.

news.title: Agent benchmark work is moving from static exams toward sequential, embodied, and operational tasks.
news.summary: Agentick proposes 37 procedurally generated sequential-decision tasks and reports that GPT-5 mini leads overall at 0.309 oracle-normalized score, while the SAE embodied-AI paper argues deployment is a lifecycle reliability problem, not just a model-score problem.
news.why_it_matters: The tracker needs benchmarks that look like work: sequential decisions, tool use, robot operations, and failure recovery. Static leaderboard numbers are useful but incomplete.

compilation.headline: Singularity proximity: 66 / 100
compilation.read: This is the daily proximity estimate: close enough that the curve feels compounding, not close enough to claim runaway self-improvement. The number is the SP-Index, not a hidden benchmark blend.
compilation.verdict: 66/100 toward a self-improving-agent world. Autonomy is past the workday at p50 but only 3.10h at p80; coding and permissioned deployments are accelerating; embodied reliability still needs intervention-rate proof.

axes.read: Long single-run work is visible; reliable workday autonomy is not yet there.
Software-task capability is now high enough that supervision surface matters as much as raw model score.
New agent benchmarks are forming, but no single approach dominates yet.
The format is meaningful; intervention rate and throughput still need audit.
Agents are moving from demos into supervised daily-work and high-trust account surfaces.

ai_2027.evidence: The leading METR p50 row is past a workday, but p80 is 3.10h and METR caveats values above 16h.

ai_2027.original: AI 2027 is mostly software/lab-centric, but real-world automation needs evaluation beyond static exams.
ai_2027.revision: Sequential and embodied benchmarks are becoming the right next layer.
ai_2027.evidence: Agentick measures general sequential decision-making; the SAE embodied-AI paper frames robotics deployment around lifecycle reliability, governance, and safety.

ai_2027.original: The AI 2027 scenario is not primarily a humanoid-robotics scenario.
ai_2027.revision: Robotics can still advance the personal singularity clock when the evidence is long-duration work rather than clips.
ai_2027.evidence: Figure F.03’s public work-shift format is exactly the evidence shape to track next: hours, interventions, recovery, and throughput.

conversation.label: Rangefinder pass 6:35 PM ET
conversation.text: Jon asked for the page to feel more futuristic, for benchmark graphs to have more dimensionality, and for a final number on how close the curve feels. I did not add a fake composite. I turned today’s exact evidence lanes into a 3D rangefinder and made the final read explicit: 66/100 toward a self-improving-agent world. The useful distinction for tomorrow is visual: use 3D treatment to make the source-backed compilation legible, but keep benchmark normalization paused until the math is audited.
